claims.claim: Kenya announced a moratorium on logging and charcoal production on 24 February 2018.
claims.episode_span: On 24 February 2018 the Kenyan government announced a moratorium on logging and charcoal production in public and community forests.
claims.source_title: The unintended consequences of production bans: the case of the 2018 Kenya logging moratorium
claims.supporting_quote: We examine the effects of Kenya’s 2018 moratorium on the extraction of wood products, including logs and charcoal, from public and community forests.

claims.claim: Domestic charcoal prices in Kenya rose 36 percent immediately after the 2018 moratorium.
claims.episode_span: Domestic charcoal prices rose 36 percent almost immediately, and charcoal imports from Uganda increased 133 percent in the first six months.
claims.source_title: The unintended consequences of production bans: the case of the 2018 Kenya logging moratorium
claims.supporting_quote: The data show an immediate 36% increase in the domestic charcoal price in Kenya.

claims.claim: Charcoal imports from Uganda to Kenya rose 133 percent in the first six months of the 2018 ban.
claims.episode_span: Domestic charcoal prices rose 36 percent almost immediately, and charcoal imports from Uganda increased 133 percent in the first six months.
claims.source_title: The unintended consequences of production bans: the case of the 2018 Kenya logging moratorium
claims.supporting_quote: we document an increase of 133% percent in charcoal imports from Uganda to Kenya during the first 6 months of the ban.

claims.claim: More than 80 percent of Kenyan consumers use charcoal as their primary energy source.
claims.episode_span: Charcoal remained the primary cooking fuel for more than 80 percent of households.
claims.source_title: The unintended consequences of production bans: the case of the 2018 Kenya logging moratorium
claims.supporting_quote: where over 80% of consumers use it as their primary energy source.
